local_memory.learning: The useful carrier transfer is not MCSP-hardness folklore but a precise interface: uniform high-MCSP truth tables at threshold N^epsilon transfer to E lower bounds and IW derandomization. The route currently fails at source construction, not at the extraction step. Nonuniform leakage is the main formal obstruction.

The repair isolates a concrete bridge: co-side gap reductions to MCSP are not just hardness evidence; with length balance and threshold N^epsilon they automatically manufacture explicit E lower bounds. Thus the route's main obstruction is quantitative source strength, not extraction. This also explains why weak MCSP reductions and nonuniform selectors are invalid for the target.

Cycle 3 identifies the missing quantitative invariant: length-balanced co-side GapMCSP reductions give valid sparse E lower bounds, but IW derandomization needs rho-dense all-length hardness. The route is therefore not blocked at extraction once density is assumed; it is blocked at constructing uniform dense no-side carriers without nonuniform leakage.

Cycle 4 sharpens the route: rho-dense all-length carriers are sufficient but not necessary. A constant-gap explicit no-side MCSP sequence already transfers to all-length E hardness with exponent delta<epsilon/gamma. Conversely, superconstant gaps or epsilon(N)->0 create a quantitative threshold collapse, and nonuniform selectors invalidate the target class.

Cycle 5 turns the vague density requirement into a proved quantitative bridge: MCSP no-side threshold 2^{epsilon m} plus carrier gap kappa gives all-length E hardness exponent any delta<epsilon/kappa. The exact obstruction is now constructive, not folklore: build a uniform constant-gap no-side carrier or the route fails by threshold collapse or nonuniform leakage.

Cycle 6 converts the route into an equivalence audit. The bridge lemma is valid and quantitatively sharp: threshold 2^{epsilon m} plus kappa-density transfers to any E lower-bound exponent delta<epsilon/kappa. The new obstruction is circularity: a uniform constant-gap MCSP no-side carrier is already an E circuit lower bound, so future progress must supply a non-natural, nonuniform-free certificate of high MCSP rather than reuse the carrier as a black box.

Cycle 7 repairs the circular carrier by making the source a searchable proof-like object. The valid bridge now has a sharp threshold: O(m)-bit sound certificates on kappa-gap source lengths yield E lower bounds with exponent delta<epsilon/kappa. The remaining task is not another hardness-magnification slogan but construction of a sparse, non-natural, nonuniform-free certificate source; dense constructive variants hit the natural-proofs falsifier.

Cycle 8 converts the certificate repair into a precise bridge theorem: O(m)-bit, 2^{O(m)}-verifiable, sound MCSP no-side certificates on kappa-dense lengths yield all-length E lower bounds with exponent delta<epsilon/kappa. The bridge is valid and non-large, but the remaining obstruction is the construction of such a verifier without circularly assuming high circuit complexity.

Cycle 9 finds a hidden witness-location gap. The valid bridge needs a uniform certificate-expander, not merely short certificates for externally supplied truth tables. With this repair, the transfer to E lower bounds is clean: threshold 2^{epsilon m} on kappa-dense source lengths gives exponent delta<epsilon/kappa. Dense external repairs are natural-proof falsifiers; brute-force soundness has a quantitative threshold collapse.

Cycle 10 adds a concrete interface theorem and a new obstruction. The valid bridge uses self-locating streaming certificates and transfers threshold 2^{epsilon m} on kappa-dense source lengths to E lower bound exponent any delta<epsilon/kappa. The hidden falsifier is subthreshold random access: a locally computable expander would itself give small circuits for the certified tables. Thus future source attempts must be sparse, non-natural, uniform, streaming, and sound without low-locality or advice.

Cycle 11 removes an unnecessary self-location demand: exhaustive uniform search over O(r)-bit certificates and the kappa-density window already locates a valid stream in E time. The new exact obstruction is random-access leakage: any bit-addressable implementation below exponent epsilon refutes the source soundness. Thus the route's valid core is a sparse, searchable, sequential-only certificate source; constructing its soundness remains the hard non-natural task.

Cycle 12 sharpens the valid transfer into a budget theorem: O(m)-bit sequential certificates and 2^{O(m)} verification are exactly compatible with E extraction at constant density, while omega(m)-bit certificates or subthreshold random access are formal falsifiers. The bridge is route-level progress only; constructing a sparse, sound, non-natural MCSP certificate source is still the hard task.

Cycle 13 gives an exact quantitative falsifier for brute-force MCSP source soundness: enumeration is E-compatible only up to s=O(m/log m), making epsilon_m=O(log m/m) and delta=o(1). The valid carrier bridge survives, but any constant-threshold source must be non-enumerative, sparse, non-natural, and nonuniform-free.

Cycle 14 adds an exact locality threshold: any accepted certificate with block access below exponent epsilon yields small circuits for its own table, so it cannot be a sound MCSP no-side carrier. The valid bridge survives, but the remaining source must be sparse, non-enumerative, non-natural in the large-property sense, nonuniform-free, and globally sequential with seek cost at least 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}.

Cycle 15 adds a precise restart-leakage threshold: sequential-only is insufficient. A valid constant-threshold MCSP source must be anti-restartable against every uniform checkpoint mechanism below 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}. This is a source-side obstruction, not progress on P != NP itself.

Cycle 16 narrows the source-side obstruction. Sequential restartability is not itself a falsifier; only subthreshold indexed restart, short local decoding, or a checkpoint storage/replay tradeoff below 2^{epsilon m} invalidates the MCSP no-side claim. This keeps the route non-large and outside the immediate natural-proofs barrier, while preserving the valid carrier-to-E transfer as route-level progress only.

Cycle 17 adds a quantitative upper-bound obstruction: any sequential certificate verifier with configuration exponent sigma automatically gives its emitted tables circuits of exponent at most (1+sigma)/2 via hardwired checkpoints. Thus a constant MCSP threshold is not merely about anti-random-access; it must also be below the universal checkpoint exponent, or the source is invalid. The carrier-to-E bridge remains valid but only after this space-sensitive threshold audit.

Cycle 18 repairs the checkpoint obstruction: the cap is not a universal (1+sigma)/2 statement but alpha_V=inf_lambda max(1-lambda+sigma,tau_V(lambda)). The route gains a valid quantitative falsifier for proposed MCSP sources and a cap-aware E-transfer ceiling delta<epsilon/kappa<=alpha_V/kappa. The remaining hard task is constructing a sparse, canonical, non-natural source with proved soundness and declared tau_V profile.

Cycle 19 isolates a certificate-length trichotomy. Short O(m)-bit MCSP certificates give a valid E-compatible, constructive but non-large carrier image. Superlinear certificates already break exhaustive E canonicalization, and near-N salt is the exact point where largeness can appear, creating a natural-proofs falsifier if constructivity is restored. Thus random-salt density repairs are quarantined; the remaining viable route is a sparse, canonical, non-natural, cap-aware short-certificate source.

Cycle 20 adds an entropy-aware checkpoint cap. The valid route is narrower: short certificates keep the carrier sparse and E-canonicalizable, but any source must satisfy epsilon<=alpha_V and cannot use salt to buy density. This is route-level progress and a falsifier for source proposals, not a proof of P != NP.

Cycle 21 turns anti-restart intuition into a concrete block-checkpoint cap. For polynomial-space linear sequential emitters, alpha_V=1/2, so any MCSP no-side claim above 2^{m/2+o(m)} is an invalid source proposal. The carrier bridge is still valid only in the window epsilon<=alpha_V and delta<epsilon/kappa; this is route-level progress and a falsifier for overstrong carriers, not progress on the main P != NP conjecture itself.

Cycle 22 finds a hidden soundness quantifier. A short MCSP carrier with existential hard witnesses is not enough: the valid bridge to E lower bounds needs every accepted table to be hard, or a uniform selector for a hard accepted table. Otherwise a contaminated easy certificate is a formal falsifier. This is route-level progress, not evidence for P != NP itself.

Cycle 23 proves the exact selector quantifier needed by the MCSP carrier route. The valid transfer is not from existence of a hard accepted certificate, but from universal hardness of accepted certificates or from a uniform selector certified to choose a hard one. Easy contamination is a concrete falsifier for weaker source claims, and brute-force MCSP postfiltering cannot repair it within E.

Cycle 24 repairs the previous selector obstruction. Existential hard accepted witnesses suffice via certificate-index multiplexing, with exact quantitative loss factor 1+c in the exponent. Easy contamination is a falsifier only for same-length extraction; the remaining hard obstruction is constructing a sparse, non-natural, cap-compatible source with constant epsilon and linear certificate length.

Cycle 25 converts the selector repair into a quantitative theorem: existential hard accepted MCSP witnesses transfer through certificate-index multiplexing with exact exponent loss 1+c, and kappa-padding gives delta<epsilon/((1+c)kappa). Easy contamination is no longer a falsifier for the multiplexed target, but superlinear certificates, nonuniform length selection, and epsilon above the verifier cap remain formal blockers. This is valid route-level progress, not a proof of P != NP.

Cycle 26 sharpens the multiplexing repair: the exponent loss is controlled by accepted-set entropy h, not raw certificate length c. Canonical lexicographic unranking is E-uniform for linear certificates, so existential hard accepted witnesses transfer without a selector and without easy-contamination failure. The remaining obstruction is now a low-entropy, cap-compatible, non-natural MCSP source with constant epsilon; unbounded accepted entropy is a valid quantitative falsifier.

Cycle 27 turns accepted-set entropy into an exact quantitative transfer parameter. The bridge is valid: existential hard MCSP witnesses suffice after multiplexing with loss 1+h and padding loss kappa. The remaining obstruction is source construction, specifically a uniform low-entropy cap-compatible non-natural certificate family with constant epsilon.

Cycle 28 separates three parameters that were partly conflated: certificate length c affects only E-uniform computation, accepted-set entropy H gives the exact multiplexing rate loss, and verifier cap alpha_V bounds the admissible source threshold epsilon. The valid bridge is delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+H)); the unresolved task is constructing a uniform low-entropy, cap-compatible, non-natural MCSP source.

Cycle 29 finds a sharper transfer parameter: accepted certificates may be numerous if their emitted tables collapse to low distinct-image entropy D by an E-canonical quotient. The valid exponent is delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)); the unresolved work is constructing such a source.

Cycle 30 closes the quotient gap left by image entropy: duplicate certificates are harmless when linear certificates allow E-canonical distinct-image unranking. The exact transfer parameter remains D, giving delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)). The new blocking obligation is source-side: prove a cap-compatible constant-epsilon MCSP hard image inside a sparse canonical image family without advice or a large constructive property.

Cycle 31 fixes the exact quotient transfer: the exponent loss is D, not certificate count, once E-canonical distinct-image unranking is available. The bridge is valid route progress; the remaining hard task is a bounded-D, cap-compatible, non-natural, no-advice MCSP source theorem.

Cycle 32 isolates the access-profile parameter. Low distinct-image entropy does not itself leak small circuits; subthreshold random access does. The valid bridge is still delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)), but the source theorem must be sequentially explicit, bounded-image, cap-compatible, no-advice, and non-counting.

Cycle 33 identifies the ranked decoder as the exact leakage interface for low-image MCSP carriers. The valid transfer remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)), but bounded-image entropy cannot count its way to hardness. A valid source theorem must give structural row-hardness without advice, or else use an external non-natural aggregate decoder lower bound; subthreshold ranked random access is a concrete falsifier.

Cycle 34 converts the ranked-decoder concern into an exact threshold theorem. Low distinct-image entropy D costs twice: it reduces the extracted E exponent to epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) and raises the aggregate lower bound needed to force row hardness to (D+epsilon)/(1+D). The route remains valid but only with a very small-D, cap-compatible, non-natural source or a genuinely unrestricted aggregate lower bound; otherwise the aggregate method is circular or falsified.

Cycle 35 identifies a sharper obstruction: low-image entropy D creates an index-hardness channel. The valid extraction exponent remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) from an actual hard row, but aggregate-only row forcing needs q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) and must also satisfy q_force<=alpha_A. Thus, with alpha_A=1/2, D<=1-2epsilon is mandatory; near the cap only D=o(1) is viable. This is route-level progress and a falsifier for aggregate shortcuts, not a proof of P != NP.

Cycle 36 establishes rank-index conservation for low-image MCSP carriers. The D overhead cannot be removed by hashing or compressed aggregates without losing row recovery or adding advice. Thus q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) is an exact aggregate-forcing threshold, while the valid E extraction from an actual hard row remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)). The viable source search is now tiny-D direct row hardness or a genuine unrestricted aggregate lower bound with declared cap slack.

Cycle 37 isolates a hidden model mismatch: aggregate row forcing is a nonuniform unrestricted statement. Uniform decoder hardness, restricted-circuit lower bounds, or index hardness do not certify MCSP rows. The exact gate is q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) with cap condition D<=(alpha_A-epsilon)/(1-alpha_A).

Cycle 38 proves the exact nonuniform aggregate-forcing gate and gives a concrete constant-row falsifier for uniform aggregate shortcuts. The bridge is valid only for unrestricted circuit lower bounds above q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D), with cap slack D<(alpha_A-epsilon)/(1-alpha_A); otherwise the route must switch to direct tiny-D row hardness.

Cycle 39 separates three exponents: q_extract=epsilon/(1+D) for direct hard-row transfer, q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) for unrestricted aggregate row-forcing, and the ranked-decoder leakage cutoff epsilon/(1+D). The valid bridge survives, but aggregate evidence is useful only above q_force with cap slack; otherwise the route must produce a tiny-D direct row-hardness certificate.

Cycle 40 adds a concrete source-side no-go theorem: subthreshold point evidence cannot certify a direct hard MCSP row, because arbitrary labels on t positions have unrestricted circuits of size O(tm). Thus the viable low-D route must find a global, non-natural, advice-free proof invariant for unrestricted row hardness; the existing extraction bridge stays valid but gains a sharper falsifier.

Cycle 41 proves an unconditional affine-invariant no-go: every nonempty rank-R affine syndrome over a truth table contains a support-at-most-R representative and hence a circuit of size O(Rm). This makes low-rank parity/checksum carriers a concrete falsifier even when they are sparse and outside the usual large natural-property barrier. The valid carrier-to-E transfer is unchanged; the source search is narrowed to nonlinear global invariants with bounded D and no advice.

Cycle 42 proves a new source-side no-go: any nonempty low-ANF-degree acceptance predicate over truth-table bits accepts a sparse table, so it cannot universally certify MCSP hardness above its ANF degree times equality-test overhead. This extends the affine-syndrome falsifier to bounded-degree nonlinear fibers and identifies high ANF degree, not mere nonlinearity, as the next required invariant.

Cycle 43 adds a necessary source parameter: zero-fill vulnerability. High ANF degree is not the real invariant; any accepted sparse table or small positive accepting certificate gives an explicit small unrestricted circuit and destroys MCSP no-side soundness. This is route-level progress and a concrete falsifier family, not evidence for P != NP itself.

Cycle 44 proves a sharper source-side falsifier: MCSP carrier soundness at threshold 2^{epsilon m} requires every accepting cylinder to have both positive and negative load above 2^{epsilon m}/Theta(m). This is valid route-level progress because it rejects zero-fill and one-fill transcript sources quantitatively. It also shows the repair is only necessary: balanced-heavy predicates still accept polynomial-size functions such as parity, so the missing object is a non-natural, advice-free, circuit-sensitive global invariant, not another balance or density condition.

Cycle 45 turns the vague warning that balance is insufficient into a quantitative no-go: any nonempty MCSP source factoring through a subthreshold rankable profile accepts a canonical low-complexity filler. The next viable source must be non-natural, advice-free, low-D, cap-compatible, and genuinely circuit-sensitive rather than a load or bucket-count invariant.

Cycle 46 adds a circuit-sensitive sparse-correction falsifier: MCSP soundness at threshold 2^{epsilon m} requires accepted rows to be Omega(2^{epsilon m}/m) far from every subthreshold circuit, not just from zero, one, or rankable profiles. This is valid route-level progress because it rejects balanced perturbation carriers while leaving the existing carrier-to-E extraction intact.

Cycle 47 formalizes the sparse-correction obstruction as bad-ball disjointness and computes the calibration bound: random low-D images robustly avoid every subthreshold correction ball with overwhelming probability. Thus the route is not blocked by combinatorics. It is blocked by producing an E-uniform, non-large, non-natural selector; lex-first and dense outside-U repairs are invalid.

Cycle 48 identifies the exact failure mode of the tempting repair from random bad-ball avoidance to explicit selectors. The combinatorial carrier exists with overwhelming probability, but derandomizing it by any succinct local decoder makes every row circuit-easy. A valid source must be low-D, no-advice, non-natural, and decoder-hard; otherwise the route either has a concrete falsifier or has already proved the aggregate lower bound it wanted to extract.

Cycle 49 adds a quantitative interval-decoder leakage theorem. The previous local-decoder falsifier extends to any indexed block restart: a source with alpha_int<epsilon cannot be an MCSP no-side carrier. Random robust low-D carriers still exist combinatorially, so the real obstruction is an E-uniform, no-advice, non-natural selector whose access profile is itself hard. The established extraction exponent delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) remains valid conditional on such a source.

Cycle 50 adds a new quantitative leakage obstruction: low-D plus smooth rank traversal is itself a circuit upper bound. Random robust carriers can be combinatorially far from all small circuits, but an explicit iterative repair path with fewer than 2^{epsilon m} cumulative hardwirable edits destroys MCSP soundness. The surviving source must be non-natural, no-advice, low-D, cap-compatible, interval-hard, and now rank-jump-hard. This is valid route-level progress only, not progress on the main P != NP conjecture.

Cycle 51 repairs the previous rank-jump claim. The exact valid obstruction is rooted edit leakage: C(T)<=C(A)+O(mP). Low-volume edits from an easy anchor falsify MCSP soundness, but unrooted smooth traversal can also propagate hardness from a hard anchor and is not by itself a proof failure. The surviving route now needs a low-D, no-advice, cap-compatible carrier with a hard row and a rooted-edit-hardness certificate.

Cycle 52 isolates the exact rooted version of rank-jump leakage. Low-D plus smooth updates is harmful only from a known easy anchor; then beta+eta<epsilon, and in rank order beta+D<epsilon, is a valid source-side falsifier. Unrooted smoothness is not enough. The established MCSP-carrier extraction remains conditional route progress, not a proof of P != NP.

Cycle 53 corrects the rooted-volume accounting: for unrestricted MCSP row hardness, a circuit may hardwire the chosen easy center and final edit list, so the leakage exponent is max(xi,eta), not beta+eta or D+eta. This strengthens the falsifier for proposed sources and identifies the real next obligation as a global anti-ball certificate. The established carrier extraction is still valid only conditionally and gives no direct proof of P != NP.

Cycle 54 converts the previous rooted-volume ambiguity into a precise diagonal anti-ball invariant. The invariant is sufficient for MCSP row hardness and transfers through low-D multiplexing with exponent delta<(epsilon-rho)/(kappa(1+D)). Random anti-ball carriers exist by a strong cover bound, but lex-first, brute-force, dense constructive, and local-decoder implementations are invalid. The remaining task is a sparse, no-advice, non-natural anti-ball certificate, not a proof of P != NP.

Cycle 55 adds a concrete lower bound against list-based anti-ball sources. Positive-radius anti-ball soundness cannot be certified by enumerating forbidden easy centers: sparse easy indicators form a super-E packing. The valid route narrows to symbolic, no-advice, non-large certificates proving distance from all unrestricted circuits. This is route-level progress and a falsifier for a certificate implementation, not evidence that P != NP is solved.

Cycle 56 contributes a concrete no-go: black-box symbolic anti-ball certification has a transcript-load threshold q=Omega(2^{epsilon m}/m). This invalidates short query-based proofs as a falsifier while preserving a valid conditional bridge for non-black-box binding certificates. It also repairs radius accounting: rho is not charged to exact MCSP extraction unless the source only forbids smaller centers or spends a sparse edit list.

Cycle 57 separates proof length from proof location. A nonblackbox anti-ball proof can be long without harming the MCSP-to-E extraction if the row/proof pair is E-uniformly generated; an existential long proof is not valid because locating it is double-exponential. The route's next hard obligation is a generated, sparse, non-large anti-ball proof family, not another hardness-magnification slogan.

Cycle 58 separates proof length from proof locatability. A generated proof may be exponentially long without reducing the carrier-to-E lower-bound exponent, provided the row/proof stream is deterministic and advice-free. The real new obstruction is projection/locator naturalness: making proofs findable for a large set of rows turns the source into a natural useful property, while indexed access still falsifies MCSP soundness. Thus the valid transfer is delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)); constructing the generated non-natural anti-ball source remains open.

Cycle 59 contributes a quantitative projection dichotomy. Low-D generated anti-ball carriers stay safely non-large under every sublinear Hamming locator repair, with measure 2^{-N+o(N)}, so the natural-proofs barrier is not triggered there. But any repair that makes the projection natural-size and poly(N)-decidable while preserving small-circuit exclusion becomes a useful natural property. Thus the next source theorem must be sparse and generated, not dense and locatable; the carrier-to-E transfer remains valid only conditionally.

Cycle 60 separates proof length from proof-generation exponent. Generated anti-ball proofs may be exponentially long without weakening the MCSP-to-E transfer, but only with a constant exponent and advice-free generation. Superconstant generation overhead is a valid quantitative falsifier because preserving E then collapses the extracted exponent to o(1). The remaining source obligation is a sparse generated non-natural anti-ball certificate against unrestricted circuits.

Cycle 62 closes a ledger gap: generated proof length is harmless, but generated proof time must have a fixed exponential rate. The bridge exponent is unchanged by constant gamma; unbounded gamma is a valid quantitative falsifier because it moves the target out of E.

Cycle 63 adds a latency ledger: constant total proof generation is not the decisive issue; the valid transfer needs constant E-time row-bit generation, while any separate indexed row opening below theta is an immediate MCSP-source falsifier. The extraction exponent remains delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)), and the unresolved work is a nonblackbox generated anti-ball source with no advice and no subthreshold openings.

Cycle 64 sharpens the generated anti-ball route: advice-free proof generation is not enough. Because MCSP hardness is nonuniform, any subthreshold proof skeleton that opens row bits can be hardwired into circuits and is a valid source falsifier. Conditional extraction remains delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)), but the source theorem must now prove unrestricted anti-ball hardness plus nonuniform-opening-hardness of its proof stream.

Cycle 65 upgrades the nonuniform-skeleton warning into an exact falsifier: compressed proof skeleton plus indexed opening below theta collapses the claimed MCSP row hardness. A valid generated source must live in the narrow window theta<=gamma=O(1) and avoid every omega<theta opener. This is route-level progress, not evidence that P != NP is solved.

Cycle 66 adds a time-space checkpoint cap to the generated anti-ball route. Avoiding indexed openings is not sufficient: a deterministic row/proof generator with small configurations and low per-output overhead gives nonuniform circuits for its own rows by hardwiring periodic configurations. The exact falsifier is theta>inf_beta max{1-beta+sigma,beta+nu}; in particular polynomial-space near-linear generated sources cannot certify MCSP hardness above 2^{m/2+o(m)}. The prior carrier-to-E transfer remains valid only after this cap audit.

Cycle 67 closes the checkpoint-profile optimization. A generated row/proof carrier with configuration exponent sigma and per-output exponent nu has a nonuniform self-circuit exponent alpha_chk=inf_beta max{1-beta+sigma,beta+nu}, with clipped closed form. Polynomial-space near-linear generators are capped at 1/2, so theta>1/2 is a valid falsifier for that implementation class. The conditional E-transfer remains delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) only when theta survives this cap.

Cycle 68 adds a sharper leakage channel than periodic checkpoints. A generated carrier can be globally sequential yet invalid if its transition is algebraically skippable: composing a skip-ahead opener with the bit decoder gives a nonuniform circuit for each row. This creates a finite falsifier for LFSR/affine/iteratable proof streams and upgrades the source obligation to noniteratable, skip-hard, advice-free anti-ball generation. The valid extraction theorem is unchanged and remains conditional route progress only.

Cycle 69 adds a covering-opener cap: any generated MCSP carrier with rankable block summaries has row circuits of exponent max{1-lambda+sigma,omega}. This is a valid finite falsifier for many non-skippable proof streams and refines the source obligation to block-summary-hard, noniteratable, advice-free anti-ball generation. The carrier-to-E transfer is unchanged but only conditional on surviving this audit.

Cycle 70 compresses several leakage channels into a single semantic block-cover exponent. Any generated MCSP carrier whose row admits short per-block summaries and a shared opener has an unrestricted circuit of exponent alpha_sem=max{1-lambda+mu,omega}. Thus a valid source must prove high semantic covering dimension; sequential, noniteratable, or advice-free generation alone is insufficient.

Cycle 71 turns semantic block-cover leakage into an exponent-normal-form statement: avoiding all such covers is equivalent, up to o(1), to the unrestricted MCSP row lower bound. This sharpens the route by converting many leakage checks into one finite falsifier gate, while preserving the distinction between a valid conditional carrier transfer and an actual proof of P != NP.

Cycle 72 upgrades the semantic-cover audit from one-level summaries to hierarchical proof streams. Recursive summaries flatten to unrestricted circuits with exponent max_i{a_i+mu_i,omega_i}; hence Merkle-like, checkpoint, or digest-based repairs are invalid whenever this exponent is below theta. The useful contribution is a sharper falsifier gate, while the positive source theorem remains open and equivalent to proving genuine row hardness by nonnatural means.

Cycle 73 upgrades the semantic-cover falsifier from hierarchical static summaries to adaptive proof-opening streams. The exact new parameter is alpha_ad=max{tau,max_l(a_l+mu_l),max_l omega_l}. Any proposed generated MCSP carrier with alpha_ad<theta is invalid as a no-side source. Escaping the falsifier requires proving high adaptive cover dimension, which is essentially the unrestricted row lower bound in non-natural normal form.
